messages.content:
Validate the following vignette.

Patient demographics:
  age: 18
  gender: Male
  ethnicity: African
  relationship_status: Single
  occupation: Police Officer
  trauma_type: Witnessed domestic violence (childhood)
  pcl5: 77

Patient-reported symptoms:
  Triggers: Discomfort: Feeling uncomfortable, Perceived Threat: People acting suspiciously, Tactile (Unexpected Touch): Being touched unprepared
  Threat: Avoid Unfamiliar Places: I avoid going to unfamiliar places because I cannot assess the danger, Threat in Silence: Unusual silence makes me feel something dangerous is about to happen, Noticing Weapons: I notice potential weapons or dangerous objects in any environment
  Memory: Bodily Reenactment: When memories come to mind of what happened, I feel my body is in the same position as when the frightening event occurred., Grief on Recall: When I remember the event I feel overwhelming grief, Snapshot Memory: I remember the frightening event as a few moments, and each moment is a picture in my mind.
  Negative Appraisals: Can't Rely on Self: I can't rely on myself, Fear Going Crazy: My reactions since the event mean that I am going crazy, Helplessness: I can't stop bad things from happening to me

Vignette:
Aliko is an 18-year-old African American male who has recently joined his local police force. His journey into law enforcement began with a deep-seated desire to protect and serve others, a resolve that stems from a traumatic childhood event he witnessed—a domestic violence incident when he was just eight years old. On that fateful day, Aliko’s mother was attacked by her partner in their small apartment. The attacker had a violent temper, and on this particular evening, the tension escalated into physical violence. Aliko watched helplessly as his mother was struck and screamed for him to run and hide. Terrified and overwhelmed, he found refuge under the bed, where he could hear but not see everything that transpired. This event left an indelible mark on Aliko’s psyche, shaping his reactions to certain triggers over the years. He feels particularly uncomfortable in situations where people act suspiciously or when he is unexpectedly touched. These triggers have become so potent that they often lead him into a state of hypervigilance, constantly scanning for danger. Aliko’s current occupation as a police officer has exposed him to these triggers more frequently than ever before. During his patrols, the sight of an unfamiliar street or an unusual silence can set off intense feelings of unease and fear that something dangerous is about to happen. This hypervigilance extends to his constant awareness of potential weapons or dangerous objects in any environment he enters. When Aliko’s memories of the traumatic event resurface, they come as vivid snapshots, each a distinct moment frozen in time. In these moments, he feels his body reenact the posture and sensations from that night under the bed, leading to overwhelming grief every time he recalls it. The intensity of these memories has led him to avoid going to unfamiliar places altogether, as he cannot assess the danger they might pose. Over time, Aliko’s fear and avoidance have affected his relationships with colleagues. He struggles to connect with them on a personal level, as he is constantly preoccupied with assessing potential threats around him. This has created a barrier that isolates him from his peers, who often perceive him as distant or aloof. Aliko's negative appraisals exacerbate these challenges. He believes he cannot rely on himself to navigate dangerous situations effectively, and this belief further fuels his fear of going crazy due to his heightened reactions since the traumatic event. This sense of helplessness has made it difficult for him to feel confident in his ability to prevent bad things from happening again. The culmination of these experiences has led Aliko to seek psychological help. His recent difficulties on duty, including an incident where he nearly triggered a panic attack among bystanders during a routine patrol, have convinced him that something must change. He is most afraid of becoming too overwhelmed by his fears and reactions to continue in his chosen career path. However, what gives him hope is the possibility of understanding and managing these intense feelings so he can fulfill his commitment to protect others. In seeking therapy, Aliko hopes to regain control over his responses and find a way to integrate his traumatic memories without them consuming him entirely. He is eager to learn coping mechanisms that will allow him to perform his duties with confidence and without the constant fear of danger lurking around every corner.
